thread:
Samir: Starting a focused perf thread — ran a set of loadbench experiments this morning comparing kernel selection + KV cache behavior for tool/function-calling workloads in JSON mode. Wanted to surface methodology and a couple surprising regressions.
Anya: Nice, high level first — synthetic or replay?
Samir: Both. We did three passes: 1) pure synthetic (stateless prompts, tunable seq len) 2) replay harness (real traffic capture from last month, ~18k sessions, ~22% tool calls) 3) hybrid where we prime KV cache with replay then run synthetic to measure steady-state.
Kelly: What were the kernel variants?
Samir: baseline fp16-fused, tiled-attn, attention-fuse-v2. Also toggled quantized int8 path for a subset.
Jordan: How did you keep apples-to-apples? those always bite you. :eyes:
Samir: Agreed. We standardized on the same request stream (seeded) for all runs, identical batching policy and warmup: 600s warmup, then 1800s measurement. We also enforced the KV cache TTL to 30m and pre-populated keys for the prime stage so cache hit-rate comparisons are comparable.
Anya: Any changes to batching heuristics?
Samir: We tested two batching policies: dynamic (latency-target 100ms, max-queue 64) and fixed-window (batch window 20ms, max-batch 128). Used the same concurrency load generator for both.
Kelly: Share the harness command you used?
Samir: Sure. Command we ran:
```
./run_loadbench
  --replay capture_2026-02-11.json
  --model gptx-3b-serve
  --kernel attention-fuse-v2
  --batching policy=dynamic,max_queue=64
  --kvcache=true
  --json-validate=true
  --retries=2
  --warmup 600
  --duration 1800
```
Jordan: Thanks — did you collect per-request validation failures?
Samir: Yes. Two important signals: validation-failures (structured JSON parse/schema mismatch), and validation-retries (automated server-side retry for toolcall to attempt deterministic fallback).
perf-bot: New benchmark artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/bench-1769501234/ (summary + raw traces) :white_check_mark:
Anya: Results TL;DR?
Samir: Key takeaways: 
- attention-fuse-v2 increased tokens/sec by ~9-11% vs baseline for long-context (>1024) sessions, but memory pressure rose ~14% and we saw 3-4% more OOM retries at peak concurrency.
- tiled-attn had slightly worse tail latency (p95 + ~7%) but saved ~8% memory vs attention-fuse-v2.
- Enabling JSON validation added ~5-8% CPU overhead and pushed p95 latency up by ~12% in dynamic batching due to synchronous schema checks.
- KV cache priming reduced token generation CPU by ~18% and improved effective throughput, but only when prefix reuse >40% in the replay set. For sessions with low prefix reuse, caching added RPC overhead and worsened p95.
Jordan: The JSON validation hit is annoying. Was validation done inline?
Samir: Yes — current prod code validates synchronously before dispatching tool calls. We instrumented an async validation patch (defer to separate worker + optimistic dispatch) in the harness and saw tail latency drop back near baseline but with a small increase in failed-toolcall retries (~1.2% absolute) because some invalid outputs slipped through.
Kelly: Any perf regressions tied to kernel selection + validation interplay?
Samir: Interesting: attention-fuse-v2 combined with synchronous validation produced the worst tails: higher memory + blocking validation = queuing spikes. The hybrid scenario (prime KV then run synthetic) revealed that with high KV hit rates, attention-fuse-v2 is fine; with low KV reuse it amplifies the validation overhead.
Anya: How reproducible are these numbers?
Samir: We ran each config 3 times and reported medians; variance was about 4-6% across runs. Raw traces are in the perf-bot artifact. Also included deterministic seed files for the replay harness.
Jordan: Any quick remediation steps?
Samir: Short term: 1) flip JSON validation to async for low-latency routes (A/B). 2) Add a KV-reuse detection heuristic — if expected reuse <30% disable priming to avoid wasted RPCs. 3) Add a canary for attention-fuse-v2 under heavy concurrent cold-cache scenarios.
Kelly: Action items for eng-runtime board?
Samir: Add tests to CI: a replay-based scenario that measures validation latency and retries; a KV-priming regression check; a kernel-selection smoke test. Also add a dashboard panel for "validation retries per 10k requests" and "KV prime hit ratio".
Anya: Can you paste a short excerpt of the perf numbers? makes it easier for the board.
Samir: Paste below (per-run medians):
```
config=attention-fuse-v2 + dynamic + kv-prime + json-validate
p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=430ms tokens/s=1250 kv_hit=78% cpu=74% mem=88%

config=baseline + dynamic + kv-prime + json-validate
p50=48ms p95=235ms p99=520ms tokens/s=1135 kv_hit=76% cpu=68% mem=77%

config=tiled-attn + fixed-window + kv-prime + json-validate
p50=50ms p95=252ms p99=560ms tokens/s=1189 kv_hit=77% cpu=66% mem=72%
```
Jordan: Those p99s are concerning — are retries driving p99?
Samir: Yes, a lot of p99 is retry storms when validation fails and clients retry immediately. We simulated real client retry behavior in the replay (exponential backoff disabled) and saw clustered retries.
Kelly: Do we need a client-side change?
Anya: Maybe, but short term server-side rate-limiting on retries + backoff hints could dampen storms.
Samir: Agreed. I've filed two follow-ups: PERF-291 (add async JSON validation experiment + A/B) and PERF-292 (add KV prime heuristic). Linking artifacts in the perf-bot message.
perf-bot: PERF-291 and PERF-292 created and linked to bench artifact.
Jordan: Great. Could someone add a succinct summary for the SRE oncall handover tomorrow? I can include mitigations if tails spike.
Samir: I'll write the oncall blurb and post in #eng-oncall with quick mitigations (disable validate synchronous flag, enable retry rate limiter) if needed.
Kelly: Thanks all. This is useful — please post the distilled charts to the eng-runtime dashboard and ping infra to provision a canary pool for attention-fuse-v2 tests. :thumbsup:
